searchText: I read https://ethresear.ch/t/using-polynomial-commitments-to-replace-state-roots/7095 today but I'm not sure how it fits with verkle trees. Do verkle trees supercede the ideas in that article? Or are they being considered for other applications? Did you check out the PEEPanEIP with Dankrad? He covers vector/polynomial commitments as well, including why KZG is not a great fit for Verkle Tries. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RGJOQHzg3UQ By the way, that's how <@&688101493978562687> supports resurrected contracts even now – by using incarnation numbers. Yeah, I remember now reading that in your docs. Thats probably where I got the name from. So when switching to verkle tries, this will also be how we will do it in the state trie, not only in the client db, due to the increased costs of deleting large chunks of state. Not yet, but it's on my watchlist! I'm intrigued about KZG not working out I don't know if you've seen this open problem by Buterin https://ethresear.ch/t/open-problem-ideal-vector-commitment/7421 which I do not know if it's still open given the claims in that thread
